title: Max-flow value equals arc-disjoint path number in a unit-capacity network
statement: Let $N$ be a network with distinguished source $x$ and sink $y$ whose capacity function takes only the values $0$ and $1$ (that is, every capacity is at most $1$), and let $f$ be a maximum flow in $N$. Then the value of $f$ equals the maximum number of arc-disjoint directed $(x,y)$-paths in $N$.
hypotheses_covered: N is a network with distinguished source x and sink y
every arc capacity is at most 1
f is a maximum flow in N
replaced:
\emph{Let \texttt{N} be a network with source \texttt{x} and sink \texttt{y} in which
each arc has unit capacity.  Then the value of a maximum flow in \texttt{N} is equal to
the maximum number \texttt{m} of arc-disjoint directed \texttt{(x, y)}-paths in
\texttt{N}.}
